member_basis: NOMINAL - a two-sash PVC centre band, sash frame + sash frame
notes: O2 IS TWO SASHES WITH ONE CENTRAL MULLION AND NO TRANSOM. Two independent photos agree and one of them is OUR OWN flat: _Survey/IMG_20260913_133523_with_wall_segments.jpg shows O2 from outside as a plain 2-pane unit, and apartment 53's b6f0 shows the same from inside with a panel radiator under the sill. ⚠ THE PATTERN IS MEASURED, THE SIZES ARE NOT. A photo settles how many sashes there are and whether a transom exists - that is topology, and it is exactly what a photo is good for. It does not settle a member width: the visible centre band scales to ~140 mm off an oblique shot with no scale reference in frame, which is +/-100 at best per standing rule 9. 120 is a nominal PVC centre band pending a tape measure. The 0.5 split is likewise the DEFAULT for a two-sash unit, not a measurement - both panes read within ~3% of equal in the exterior photo, which is inside the reading error either way.

notes: O3 IS A 2x2: ONE CENTRAL MULLION AND ONE TRANSOM, four panes. The clearest evidence in the whole survey - ext1 catches it almost square-on from outside, on OUR flat, and apartment 53's bdc7 shows the same four panes from inside. Same nominal-size caveat as O2. ⚠ The exterior photo reads the right pane ~17% wider than the left, which at 1763 is ~40 mm; that is inside the reading error of an oblique shot, so 0.5 stands as the default rather than 0.46/0.54 being adopted from pixels.

position_basis: fraction of the opening's clear height
notes: ⚠ THE TWO PHOTOS DISAGREE ABOUT THE TRANSOM HEIGHT AND THE EXTERIOR ONE WINS. ext1, viewed nearly square-on, puts it within ~3% of mid-height. bdc7, oblique and from inside, reads 57/43 - the upper pane taller. An oblique interior shot compresses the far part of a vertical division, so the near-frontal view is the better instrument and 0.5 is recorded. Worth a tape measure before anything depends on it: at a 1985 opening the two readings differ by ~140 mm.

position_basis: fraction of the opening's clear width - the recorded leaf widths, not a guess
notes: O4 IS A COMBINED UNIT: A WINDOW LEAF AND A FULL-HEIGHT DOOR LEAF divided by one frame mullion - which is what wall_openings.csv has always said (O4a window, sill 735; O4b door, sill 0) and what 9db4 shows. The 0.4348 is 600 / 1380, the recorded leaf widths, so the mullion position here is NOT from the photo. !! THE DOOR LEAF IS ON THE EAST SIDE, and that is the one handedness call in this table. 9db4 is a MIRRORED flat, so its left/right cannot be carried across. What CAN be carried is a mirror-invariant relationship: in the photo the door leaf sits on the side with the SHORT wall reveal and the window leaf on the side with the long run. In our flat O4 spans x 4351.0..5731.0, leaving 1120.1 to G4a on the west and 325 to G8 on the east - so the short reveal is EAST, and the door goes east. Reading a mirrored photo through a relationship that survives mirroring is the only safe way to use one.
